svg.aria-label: Zenflow queue design: producers, three BullMQ queues on a noeviction Redis, consumers, and the lifecycle of a job including retry, breaker parking and the dead-letter queue
svg.title: Zenflow queue design: producers, three BullMQ queues on a noeviction Redis, consumers, and the lifecycle of a job including retry, breaker parking and the dead-letter queue
svg.text: One job id = one unit of work: re-enqueueing the same id is a no-op while the earlier job still exists. Every queue call is bounded by QUEUE_ENQUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS (2 s).
claims due schedule rows (CAS), enqueues one job each
id scheduleId_dueAt · first failure → hand claims back, stop
attempts 1 · API waits ≤ 25 s on QueueEvents
id push_{notificationId}_{provider} · fcm and apns separately
delay = time to fire + 5–10 s jitter, never after the start
rows 1 min – 2 h old with no push job → re-enqueue
repairs an enqueue that was dropped while Redis was down
concurrency 1 per replica · limiter: 1 job start / 750 ms across all replicas
concurrency 10 per replica · limiter 50 jobs / s across replicas
jobs: push (one provider per job), reminder (delayed)
the LRU instances would evict jobs; the pub/sub instance keeps nothing
a lost enqueue is repaired by re-derivation: ticker rows, reminder sweep, reconcileRecent
pass ok:false is recorded and the job completes
manual jobs: defer sibling kinds, or mark failure
kill switch "notifications" → drop job, no retry
SIGTERM → workers drain in-flight jobs (25 s default, 50 s in prod)
then force-close; an interrupted job is retried via the stalled check
A JOB'S LIFE (QueueService defaults: attempts 5, exponential backoff from 5 s)
What counts as a final failure
attempts used up (5) · UnrecoverableError (push job without
a provider) · stalled more than maxStalledCount (1)
Stalled jobs never emit "failed" on the worker, so each
consumer also listens on QueueEvents and runs the same
path (DLQ copy, metric, hook). Hooks are idempotent
because several replicas can see the same stalled job.
Not failures: a pass that ran and reported ok:false, a
job parked behind an open breaker, a kill-switch drop.
